content: Cefdinir capsules should be used to treat or prevent infections caused by bacteria that are proven or strongly suspected to be susceptible to this antibiotic. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or modification of therapy. In the absence of such data, local patterns of bacterial resistance and epidemiology should be considered when choosing an empiric treatment. Cefdinir is indicated for the treatment of mild to moderate infections caused by specific susceptible microorganisms in the following conditions: For Adults and Adolescents: 1. Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Cefdinir is effective against Haemophilus influenzae (including strains that produce beta-lactamase), Haemophilus parainfluenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae (only penicillin-susceptible strains), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). 2. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Cefdinir is indicated for infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Haemophilus parainfluenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae (only penicillin-susceptible strains), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). 3. Acute Maxillary Sinusitis: Cefdinir is effective against Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae (only penicillin-susceptible strains), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). Note: For pediatric use in this condition, refer to the specific pediatric indications and dosage guidelines. 4. Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis: Cefdinir is effective in eradicating Streptococcus pyogenes from the oropharynx. However, it has not been studied for the prevention of rheumatic fever following S. pyogenes pharyngitis or tonsillitis. Only intramuscular penicillin has been proven effective for preventing rheumatic fever. 5. Uncomplicated Skin and Skin Structure Infections: Cefdinir is indicated for infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus (including beta-lactamase-producing strains) and Streptococcus pyogenes. For Pediatric Patients: 1. Acute Bacterial Otitis Media: Cefdinir is effective against Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae (only penicillin-susceptible strains), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). 2. Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis: Cefdinir is effective in eradicating Streptococcus pyogenes from the oropharynx. However, similar to adults, it has not been studied for the prevention of rheumatic fever following S. pyogenes pharyngitis or tonsillitis. Only intramuscular penicillin has been demonstrated to prevent rheumatic fever. 3. Uncomplicated Skin and Skin Structure Infections: Cefdinir is indicated for infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus (including beta-lactamase-producing strains) and Streptococcus pyogenes.
